ai_technology: LASSO-Cox, ridge/elastic-net Cox and CoxBoost survival learning

evidence.ai_role: Learned survival models prioritize genes for prognostic association analysis; language assistants did not conduct scientific analysis.
evidence.tested: Existing TCGA development data and separate GEO cohort survival associations; heterogeneous endpoints and moderate discrimination.
evidence.unknown: Association is not uniformly significant across cohorts or causal; one spatial specimen and exploratory protein-image comparisons constrain interpretation. Drug-response estimates are predictions.

source_review.scope: Primary full manuscript Methods, Results, validation protocol and limitations independently reviewed.

summary: A study used penalized Cox models and CoxBoost to prioritize NFKB1 for retrospective colorectal-cancer survival analysis. Higher expression was associated with favorable survival in selected external cohorts, but the adjusted association was not significant in TCGA-COAD. Model discrimination was modest: the best overall mean time-dependent AUC was 0.650. A separate spatial analysis used one tissue specimen and does not establish macrophage-specific causality. NFKB1 remains an exploratory association, without a validated clinical cutoff or demonstrated treatment benefit.
title: Survival learning prioritizes cohort-specific NFKB1 associations in colorectal cancer
